clue.text: Unequipped to cross frozen water plain

indicators.note: one thing crossing another passes through its middle, so a word sits inside another

parts.note: not able: lacking the means to do something
frozen water is ice

explanation.surface: Someone without crampons is unable to walk over a frozen lake on flat land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a flat landscape but is the adjective meaning obvious; 'Unequipped' splits into two words around the frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain, in the sense of obvious or evident, is easily noticed.

clue.text: Zero time used up around noon

indicators.note: in a down clue, something brought up reads from the bottom upwards
around says one piece wraps the other on both sides

parts.note: an eon is a vast stretch of time
N is the standard abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: No time is left at all, the day having run out around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: EON is turned upwards to NOE, which then wraps N.
explanation.definitionFit: None means not any, the same quantity as zero.

clue.text: Object about channel getting sensational

indicators.note: about places one word on both sides of another, enclosing it

parts.note: an object is a thing
a rill is a small stream or channel

explanation.surface: A television channel is touted as producing something sensational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television, but here it is a small watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrilling event is exciting, which is what sensational means in its loose sense.

clue.text: Bond feature with adult content

indicators.note: content is what a thing holds, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A James Bond film is advertised as having adult content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' and 'adult content' conjure 007 films; Bond is simply a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a tie or bond, literally or figuratively, as in the chains that bind.

clue.text: Mean state is on decline

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: A grumble that some state's mean figure is falling.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of values.

clue.text: Tight lines dressing, say, curvy figure

indicators.note: dressing something means wrapping it, so the outer letters clothe the inner one

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural
e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
ess is the name of the letter S, a curvy shape

explanation.surface: Tight lines of fabric dress a curvy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' reads as close-fitting clothing; it is British slang for drunk. The 'curvy figure' is the letter S, spelt out as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for very drunk, and tight is a milder slang word for being drunk.

clue.text: Old French artist practically flipped

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so the letters run backwards
practically means nearly all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly French painter is said to have nearly lost his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: DEGAS loses its last letter, then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged is a straightforward synonym for old, describing someone advanced in years.

clue.text: Enjoyment is over following sudden wind

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the piece named first in the clue is placed second

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Pleasure is finished once a sudden wind arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places O after GUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty relish or enjoyment in doing something.

clue.text: Circle clearing without a sound

parts.note: a disc is a flat circle

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is taken out

parts.note: clearing, as in clearing a profit, is earning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ring of trees in a woodland clearing stands silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a sound' reads as silence; in fact EARNING drops its A, and 'sound' is the definition, as in sound judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound judge is wise and perceptive, which is what a discerning person shows.

clue.text: Show hat worn by sailors, maybe

indicators.note: a garment worn by people goes around them, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a panama is a straw hat
OR, other ranks, are non-commissioned servicemen; ordinary sailors are an example

explanation.surface: A display of a hat worn by sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors suggest AB or RN; here they are one kind of OR, other ranks, which the panama encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide view or pictorial representation laid out to be shown, and Panorama is a BBC current-affairs show.

clue.text: Quickly passed rejected estimate for recount

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: ran: moved quickly past
to rate is to estimate or assess

explanation.surface: An estimate was hastily approved and then thrown out, prompting a recount, as at an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recount' suggests counting votes again; here it means tell a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: Spectacles presented by good girls

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A pair of spectacles shown off by well-behaved girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses is the everyday word for spectacles worn to correct vision.

clue.text: Draw out some caramel on gateau

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used

parts.note: the run of letters spans the three words

explanation.surface: Instructions for piping caramel decoration across a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw out' sounds like a pastry or sugar technique; it means lengthen.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate something is to stretch or lengthen it, to draw it out.

clue.text: Bracing air from area with oxygen

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Fresh, invigorating air comes from a place rich in oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply puts O alongside ZONE; it goes in front. Ozone is the British colloquial name for fresh seaside air.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday British usage ozone means fresh, invigorating air, especially at the seaside.

clue.text: Seeming old and wise taking time

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: taking in something means absorbing it, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: sensible means wise or prudent
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone appears to be elderly and wise, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes in after the first letter of SENSIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or professed, how things seem rather than how they are.

clue.text: Upset runner losing international championship

parts.note: a ski is a runner, like a sledge's

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a title is a championship
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: An athlete is distraught after losing an international championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it is a ski. TITLE loses I.
explanation.definitionFit: To skittle is to knock over, as skittles are bowled down, so it can mean upset.

clue.text: Caricaturist raves, typically about caricature

indicators.note: the solution lies about the words, lurking among their letters

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A cartoonist gushes, as is typical, about a cruel lampoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'caricature' in the clue looks like part of the hidden source but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque or absurd imitation, a mocking caricature.

clue.text: Hone small instrument case for Elton

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the harp is a musical instrument

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: Practising on a small instrument case belonging to Elton John.
explanation.definitionFit: To hone a blade is to sharpen it on a whetstone.

clue.text: Victorian English assuming repugnant birthright

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so one word takes another into itself

parts.note: a prig is a priggish, prudish moraliser, the Victorian stereotype
E is the abbreviation for English
vile means repugnant

explanation.surface: A stuffy Victorian Englishman takes on a repellent sense of entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' is an adjective on the surface but stands for a prig, someone primly self-righteous. PRIG plus E encloses VILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthright is a privilege or advantage someone is entitled to by birth.

clue.text: State of organ after tip's cut

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: the tip of something is its end
a gland is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A medical report on the condition of an organ after its tip has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition, but means a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: England is a country, one of the constituent nations of the UK, and so a state.

clue.text: Shame lifeless sweetheart embracing vacuous geezer

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: lifeless means dead

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside letters are removed, leaving the outside

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain once the word is emptied
the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A dead lover's embrace of an empty-headed geezer brings disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like a lover but is read as sweet-heart, the centre of that word; it comes last despite appearing earlier. A geezer is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone is to humiliate or bring shame on them.

clue.text: Genuine singing periodically for group again

parts.note: genuine means real

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A band reunites for real, singing now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' suggests a band; here it is a verb meaning to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign things is to arrange or line them up afresh, regrouping them.

clue.text: Energy supplier connected to star, perhaps

parts.note: re means concerning, connected to
a star is one kind of actor, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A power company has signed up a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' tempts towards the sun as an energy source, but it is a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor generates power, so it supplies energy.

clue.text: Quiet beer is what produces gas?

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A joke that drinking beer quietly is what causes wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: beer causing gas is the surface, but the rock yields shale gas through fracking.
explanation.definitionFit: Shale is the sedimentary rock from which shale gas is extracted.

clue.text: Square generation accepts rise of Queen

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an age is a generation or era

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word reads upwards, so its letters turn round

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned generation welcomes the Queen's ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' reads as fuddy-duddy, but is the verb as in square with.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that square with each other are consistent, that is they agree.

clue.text: Attack family over son then hide

parts.note: go at: to attack
S is the abbreviation for son
kin are family

explanation.surface: Assault the household, overcome the boy, then go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family over son' means KIN comes after S. 'Hide' looks like a verb for escaping, but is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatskin is the hide or leather of a goat.

clue.text: Southern Asian robes in silk, initially

definitions.text: Southern Asian robes in silk, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its first letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: South Asian garments made of silk at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the five words spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saris are the draped robes worn by women in South Asia, often made of silk.

clue.text: Quarrel seen in bar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quarrel is a short heavy crossbow arrow
second meaning: a sliding rod used to fasten a door

explanation.surface: A row breaks out in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' looks like an argument, but it is a crossbow arrow; 'bar' looks like a pub, but is a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow arrow and a door's sliding fastener are both called by the same four-letter word.

clue.text: Covering for head of the clergy?

definitions.text: Covering for head of the clergy?

parts.words: Covering for head of the clergy?
parts.note: surface reading: someone standing in for the leader of the church
setter's reading: a cap worn on the head by members of the clergy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering for' suggests deputising for a senior cleric; it is literally headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square stiff cap worn by Roman Catholic priests and other clergy.

clue.text: Bombshell split party holding power

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it within, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: tore: ripped, split
a do is a party
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Shocking news: a party has split while in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bombshell' reads as shocking news; it is a literal explosive missile. TORE plus DO holds P.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile, an explosive shell launched at ships.

clue.text: Drain taking top off jug

indicators.note: removing the top of a word means its first letter is dropped

parts.note: a sewer is a drain

explanation.surface: Pouring something down the drain after removing the lid of a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed jug, traditionally used with a washbasin.

clue.text: Observe gathering terror, occasionally looking back

indicators.note: gathering means drawing in, so one word takes the other inside

parts.note: to observe a rule is to respect it

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Watching dread build, now and then glancing over one's shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking back' seems to describe nervous glances, but it is the definition, a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is a survey or review of past events, the act of looking back.
